- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after recent high prices, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing true price momentum; true price movements often outpace or reverse forecast trends by day 10–15.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate sharp reversals or corrections after over-optimistic peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 5–10 days, failing to capture late-stage price surges or corrections.
- Model exhibits bias toward lower values when recent history includes low prices, underreacting to subsequent rebounds.
- Overshooting after spikes is common, especially when the spike is followed by a sustained upward trend — model fails to adjust downward momentum.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to underestimating late-stage volatility, particularly in the final 10–15 days.
